transcript:
Meeting header: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment discovery - Acme Health
Date: 2025-06-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Dr. Emily Carter (CTO, Acme Health), Mark Ruiz (Head of Infrastructure), Laura Chen (InfoSec Lead), Raj Patel (Compliance)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan Lee, AE at Redwood. With me is Priya Shah, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Emily: Doing well, thanks. We'll jump right in — we have a lot to cover around air-gapped requirements.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. Quick agenda: understand your constraints (network/hardware/policy), explain Redwood's private on-prem options and air-gapped workflows, then align on next steps and any PoC needs.
[00:22] Mark: Sounds good. Just to frame — Acme Health runs in a regulated environment, no outbound internet from the core data center, and updates have to go through change control. We're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. The focus today is Private, specifically fully air-gapped deployments.
[00:36] Priya: Thanks, Mark. Quick question up front — do you have a preferred hardware profile? GPUs, drivers, that sort of thing?
[00:43] Mark: We have a mixed fleet. Primary nodes are older A100 40GB machines, some newer A100 80s in a DR cluster, and a couple of H100s in testing. We also have a set of A10s on prem for less intensive workloads.
[00:56] Laura: And from security: no outbound registry pulls, no direct contact with vendor control planes. Everything that goes onto the cluster must be vetted, checksummed, and signed. We use a hardware HSM for our KMS.
[01:10] Jordan: Understood. That's pretty typical for healthcare. Priya, do you want to sketch how our air-gapped packaging works?
[01:16] Priya: Sure. So Redwood Private can be deployed with two options: a customer-managed control plane that's entirely in your network, or a packaged air-gapped bundle. For fully air-gapped, we produce a signed artifact bundle — container images, helm charts, operators, and optional model artifacts — delivered as tarballs or via a physically shipped storage device.
[01:34] Priya: The bundle includes signatures and checksums. The upgrade path is an offline upgrade script that verifies signatures (we support both GPG and PKCS7) and optionally consults a local signed manifest. For key management, we support integrating with customer HSMs (PKCS#11) and YubiHSMs — we can configure the runtime to use your KMS for envelope keys.
[01:56] Raj: Does that mean you require any outbound callback to Redwood for licensing or telemetry?
[02:02] Priya: No outbound callbacks are required. We can run entirely offline. The control plane components that provide telemetry are optional; if you need observability we can run a local Redwood Console instance that writes audit logs locally and can export CSVs for your SIEMs.
[02:16] Laura: How do you handle SSO in an air-gapped environment? We rely on Okta/SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[02:22] Jordan: Good question. There are two patterns: if your IdP is reachable from the air-gapped network, we can configure SAML as usual. If not, we support a service-account model and local directory sync, or an SSO proxy that you host within your environment that handles SAML and issues local tokens to the Redwood control plane. Priya can share the exact options.
[02:40] Priya: Right. We have customers who run a local SAML bridge or a SCIM sync agent that runs in the DMZ and writes to an internal LDAP. For strict offline setups we suggest the service account approach with RBAC tied to your AD/LDAP.
[02:53] Mark: What about model weights? Some of the open models we're evaluating are huge — multiple hundreds of gigabytes. Can you ship weights in the bundle? Also, how does the runtime handle quantized weights to save space?
[03:05] Priya: We can include model weights in the air-gapped bundle. For very large models, we recommend quantized variants (int8 or int4 where acceptable) to reduce size. Redwood's runtime supports quantized execution paths and KV caching so you can run larger-context models more efficiently. For stateful workloads we also support sharded weights that are unpacked on-node.
[03:26] Laura: Any signing for the model artifacts themselves? We need to ensure provenance.
[03:29] Priya: Yes — model artifacts can be signed and checksummed in the manifest. We also support reproducible manifests referencing model hash IDs.
[03:36] Raj: Patch management: our change control requires an offline upgrade checklist and rollback plan. How are upgrades performed?
[03:42] Priya: Upgrades are performed via the offline bundle plus a pre-check script. The script verifies environment compatibility (OS, drivers, Nvidia driver versions), checks signatures, runs schema migration steps, and then applies changes via a controlled operator. There's a rollback mode that preserves previous container images in a local registry. We'll share a detailed upgrade playbook.
[04:03] Mark: Drivers — we are at Nvidia driver 525 on most nodes. Any minimums?
[04:08] Priya: For A100/H100 we recommend driver 515+ and CUDA 11.8+ for optimal performance; H100 may have higher minimums. We'll validate against your baseline. For older GPUs like T4 or A10 there are supported configurations but throughput will differ.
[04:23] Emily: On compliance, can you produce audit logs that show who queried what model and when, and export them to our SIEM?
[04:30] Jordan: Yes — the local console can capture audit trails, token-level logs, and per-request metadata. We can export logs in syslog/JSON and hook into your SIEM.
[04:40] Laura: Encryption at rest — everything must be encrypted with our keys. How do you store model keys and secrets?
[04:46] Priya: We support using your KMS/HSM for wrapping keys. Secrets and keys can be stored encrypted and wrapped by keys in your HSM. The node-level storage is encrypted at rest and we integrate with customer KMS for key rotation.
[04:59] Raj: Any known blockers with air-gapped updates and HSM integration? We need to know risks up front.
[05:04] Priya: Biggest friction is usually driver mismatches and local registry setup. Also sometimes customers need to adapt their change control window to allow model unpacking and cache warm-up. For HSM integration we ask for a test HSM instance for validation — PKCS#11 interface is preferred.
[05:18] Mark: Network requirements — we still have internal DNS and time sync, but no outbound DNS. Are there any hidden dependencies?
[05:24] Priya: We require internal DNS and NTP. The installer validates kernel modules for NVidia and checks for cgroups/container runtime compatibility. No outbound traffic is required unless you opt into telemetry or license key verification (which can be done manually).
[05:37] Jordan: Quick note on performance: for low latency SLOs you may want Dedicated pools per model type. Even on-prem, you can carve GPUs for predictable latency. We can show throughput profiles from similar healthcare customers.
[05:50] Emily: For PoC — we'd like to run a small benchmark with a quantized LLM on an A100 80GB and compare latency to our current on-prem transformer. What's the next step for that?
[05:59] Priya: We can run a benchmark in three ways: 1) a remote test in Redwood infra (not viable for you), 2) a seeding PoC where we ship a minimal air-gapped bundle and you run locally, or 3) Redwood-internal engineer comes on-site. Usually #2 is fastest: we provide the bundle, test scripts, and measurement harness.
[06:17] Mark: Shipping a bundle is fine. We'll need a signed manifest and an MD5/sha256 we can verify.
[06:22] Priya: We'll include sha256 and GPG signatures.
[06:25] Laura: Can you share SOC2/ISO docs? We have a vendor questionnaire.
[06:29] Jordan: Absolutely — we'll share the security pack. For air-gapped customers we also include an ATO checklist template.
[06:36] Raj: Licensing model question — do you meter per-token in an air-gapped deployment? How does billing work if there's no outbound reporting?
[06:43] Jordan: We support multiple licensing options for private deployments: a fixed capacity reserved contract, or a usage-based model with offline usage reporting. For offline reporting, the runtime generates signed usage manifests which you can upload to a portal or share via your procurement process. We can be flexible depending on your procurement constraints.
[07:02] Mark: Any recommendations on model variants to reduce storage? We're evaluating a 70B and a 13B model.
[07:08] Priya: The 13B quantized int8 is often a sweet spot for latency and footprint — much easier for air-gapped shipments. For the 70B, sharded weights and int8 can still work but you'll need more node memory and NVMe for caching. We'll include recommendations in the BOM.
[07:23] Emily: OK, sounds good. Let's talk timeline — we need a PoC within 3-4 weeks ideally. What's realistic?
[07:30] Priya: If you provide GPU inventory and an engineer to run the bundle, we can prepare the air-gapped package in about one week and the customer can deploy in 1-2 days; validation and a basic benchmark can be completed in the following week. So 3-4 weeks is reasonable.
[07:45] Jordan: To recap action items: Jordan will send the air-gapped spec, rack/BOM, and security pack; Priya will produce the offline upgrade playbook and bundle checklist; Mark will share GPU inventory and OS baseline; Laura/Raj will share compliance questions. We'll schedule the SE deep dive the week of 2025-06-23.
[07:59] Mark: That works. One more thing — do you support running without GPUs for smaller models? We have some CPU-only nodes for low-risk features.
[08:07] Priya: Yes — we support CPU execution for smaller models, though performance will be much slower. We can include a CPU fallback profile in the PoC.
[08:15] Laura: Any gotchas around air-gapped license keys or time-limited tokens?
[08:19] Jordan: We use signed license manifests that are time-bound; for offline we can issue long-lived signed entitlements and document renewal steps.
[08:28] Emily: Thanks, everyone. This was helpful. We'll wait for the spec and then coordinate internally.
[08:33] Jordan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invite for the SE deep dive.

End notes: timestamps above are approximate; some sections had cross-talk and short clarifications not fully captured by auto-transcript. Recorded duration ~62 minutes.

Attachments referenced: "air-gapped-deployment-spec.pdf" (to be sent), "security-pack.zip" (SOC2/ISO artifacts), "upgrade-playbook.pdf", benchmark harness script (link), signed artifact manifest sample.
